## First: the scan you pasted was empty, and that wasn't the fixture being clean

`evals/fixtures/04-monorepo/` contained exactly one file — `.crimes-eval-meta.json`. It's an OSS-clone fixture (egoist/tsup @ `c5e9cd9`, v8.5.1) that `pnpm evals:setup` had never materialized. Coverage confirms it: `files_total: 1`, `universal_only_by_extension: {".json": 1}`. Zero findings was a correct scan of an empty directory, not a verdict on the code.

I ran `pnpm run evals:setup` (cloned 02/03/04 — all gitignored, working tree still clean) and re-scanned. Real numbers: **92 findings** across 62 files, **24 in your three target files**.

```
name_behavior_mismatch   4   rollup.ts:38, rollup.ts:77, index.ts:167, index.ts:291
option_bag_junk_drawer   1   rollup.ts:38
return_shape_roulette    3   esbuild/svelte.ts:9, :17, :31
swallowed_error          1   rollup.ts:187
direct_date              1   rollup.ts:164
large_function          10   (structural, listed below)
large_file               1   index.ts
sync_io_in_hotpath       1   index.ts:121
```

---

## Group 1 — `return_shape_roulette` (svelte.ts): 3 findings, 1 underlying cause

All three fire on the same nest: `sveltePlugin` (L9), its `setup` (L17), and the `onLoad` callback (L31). The detector attributes nested returns to every enclosing function, so treat this as **one issue reported three times**, not three problems.

The actual shapes inside `onLoad` (L31–121):

| Line | Shape |
|---|---|
| 37 | `{ errors: [{ text }] }` — svelte not installed |
| 117 | `{ contents, warnings }` — success |
| 119 | `{ errors: [convertMessage(error)] }` — compile threw |

Plus `convertMessage` returning `{ text, location }` where `location` is `undefined` when `start`/`end` are absent, and the inline `script` preprocessor returning `{ code }` vs `{ code, map }`.

**What an agent gets wrong today:** none of these functions carries a return annotation. `convertMessage` takes `({ message, start, end }: any)` — an agent adding a fourth branch has nothing to check itself against, and TypeScript will accept `{ contents, errors: [...] }` (esbuild's `OnLoadResult` makes every field optional), which esbuild silently treats as a *failure with contents attached*. The "0% key overlap" the detector reports is real but benign here; the danger isn't shape divergence, it's that **no shape is declared at all**.

**Proposal — annotate, don't restructure.** esbuild already ships the union types; adopting them is the whole fix.

```ts
import type { OnLoadResult, OnResolveResult, Message, Plugin } from 'esbuild'

build.onResolve({ filter: /\.svelte\.css$/ }, (args): OnResolveResult => …)
build.onLoad({ filter: /\.svelte$/ }, async (args): Promise<OnLoadResult> => …)

// and replace the `any`:
type SvelteMessage = { message: string; start?: Position; end?: Position }
const convertMessage = ({ message, start, end }: SvelteMessage): Message => …
```

Effort: quick. This makes the "errors and contents are mutually exclusive" rule enforceable and kills the `any` that currently launders Svelte's error object into esbuild's `Message` slot unchecked.

---

## Group 2 — `name_behavior_mismatch`: 4 findings, and only one is worth acting on

**`getRollupConfig` (rollup.ts:38) — true positive, fix it.** First statement in the body is `setSilent(options.silent)`, a module-global mutation in `log.ts`. It also does async I/O (`loadPkg`, `getProductionDeps`). A `get*` name on a function that mutates global logging state is exactly the trap the detector is for: an agent that calls it to *inspect* the config — say, to add a `--print-config` flag — silently reconfigures the logger for the rest of the process.

Proposal: hoist the side effect to the caller. `startRollup` (L216) is the only call site.

```ts
const startRollup = async (options: NormalizedOptions) => {
  setSilent(options.silent)              // caller owns the side effect
  const config = await getRollupConfig(options)   // now genuinely a getter
  …
}
```

**`buildStart` (rollup.ts:77) — false positive, suppress it.** This is Rollup's plugin lifecycle hook name. It is not renameable and calling `removeFiles` is its entire purpose. The detector's "name prefix suggests a pure transformation" heuristic doesn't know about framework-mandated hook names.

**`build` (index.ts:167) and `buildAll` (index.ts:291) — noise, don't rename.** `build` is the package's primary export. In a build tool, "build" naming a side-effecting operation is the correct name, not a misleading one. The detector reads `build*` as a pure-transformation prefix; that heuristic is miscalibrated for this domain. Both cite `removeFiles` as the sole side-effect signal, which is the `--clean` implementation working as designed.

If you own the crimes detector, that 2-of-4 false-positive rate on this file is the actionable output here: `buildStart`/`buildEnd`/`transform`/`load`/`resolveId` on an object literal assigned to a `Plugin`-typed binding should be exempt, and `build` probably shouldn't be in the pure-prefix set at all.

---

## Group 3 — `option_bag_junk_drawer` (rollup.ts:38): right smell, wrong diagnosis

The finding says `getRollupConfig` "accepts a broad `options` object with an **implicit** shape." That's inaccurate — the signature is `options: NormalizedOptions`, fully typed. Same for the three out-of-scope hits (`main`, `runEsbuild`).

The real problem is one level up: `Options` in `options.ts` has **73 declared fields**, and every consumer takes the whole thing. `getRollupConfig` reads 10 of them (`cjsInterop`, `clean`, `dts`, `entry`, `external`, `format`, `outDir`, `outExtension`, `silent`, `watch`); `runEsbuild` reads 38.

**What an agent gets wrong today:** adding a dts-only option means editing the 73-field god-type, and nothing tells you which of the four consumers is supposed to honor it. Nothing fails if you add the field and wire it into zero of them.

**Proposal — narrow at the parameter, not the definition.** Don't split `Options` (it's the public config surface and users type against it). Narrow what each consumer *declares* it needs:

```ts
type DtsBuildOptions = Pick<NormalizedOptions,
  | 'cjsInterop' | 'clean' | 'dts' | 'entry' | 'external'
  | 'format' | 'outDir' | 'outExtension' | 'silent' | 'watch'>

const getRollupConfig = async (options: DtsBuildOptions): Promise<RollupConfig> => …
```

Now the compiler answers "which options affect the dts build?" and an agent adding an option gets a type error at the consumer that forgot it. Zero runtime change.

**Bonus the scanner didn't flag:** `rollup.ts:33` exports `type RollupConfig = { inputConfig; outputConfig }`, and `watchRollup` (L193) redeclares that exact shape inline instead of using it. `runRollup` uses the named type. Two spellings of one contract in one file — trivially unified, and the kind of drift that grows.

---

## Group 4 — `swallowed_error` (rollup.ts:187): the one real bug in this cluster

Ranked lowest by the scanner (`agent_risk` 0.27), but it's the most dangerous thing in these files.

```ts
async function runRollup(options: RollupConfig) {
  try { … } catch (error) {
    handleError(error)                    // sets process.exitCode = 1,
    logger.error('dts', 'Build error')    // posts 'error' to parentPort
  }                                       // …then returns NORMALLY
}

const startRollup = async (options: NormalizedOptions) => {
  …
  try {
    await runRollup(config)
    parentPort?.postMessage('success')     // ← always reached, even on failure
  } catch { parentPort?.postMessage('error') }   // ← unreachable
}
```

`runRollup` never rethrows, so `startRollup`'s `catch` is dead code and `postMessage('success')` fires on every dts failure. This doesn't currently break the build only because `handleError` posts `'error'` first (`errors.ts:34`) and the listener in `index.ts:240` terminates the worker on the first message it sees — the stray `'success'` lands after termination.

**That is load-bearing message ordering with nothing documenting it.** An agent that "cleans up" `handleError` by moving the `parentPort.postMessage` out, or that makes the listener non-terminating to collect diagnostics, converts every dts failure into a green build.

**Proposal:**

```ts
async function runRollup(options: RollupConfig): Promise<void> {
  try { … } catch (error) {
    handleError(error)
    logger.error('dts', 'Build error')
    throw error                    // let startRollup own the messaging
  }
}
```

and drop the `parentPort.postMessage('error')` out of `handleError` so worker-protocol messages originate from exactly one place. Do this **first** — it's the only change here that fixes a correctness hazard rather than a readability one.

---

## Sequencing

1. **`swallowed_error` in `rollup.ts`** — real bug, currently masked by message ordering.
2. **`setSilent` hoist out of `getRollupConfig`** — one call site, removes the genuine name/behavior lie.
3. **Return-type annotations in `svelte.ts`** — mechanical, uses esbuild's own types, kills an `any`.
4. **`Pick`-narrowed parameter types + collapse the duplicate `RollupConfig`** — no runtime change, biggest payoff for future agent edits.
5. **Suppress `buildStart`, `build`, `buildAll`** as detector noise, or fix the heuristic upstream.

The 10 `large_function` findings (`build` at 293 lines, `mainTasks` at 194, `setup` at 106) are the reason all of the above is hard to see in the first place, but splitting them is a much larger change than the type-tightening you asked for and I'd keep it out of this pass.

One caveat on the whole plan: this is a vendored upstream fixture. If the intent was to evaluate crimes' output rather than to actually patch tsup, edits here will be blown away by the next `evals:setup` on a fresh checkout.
